<div id="rmarkdown-into-github-pages" class="section level1">
<h1>R Markdown into GitHub Pages</h1>
<p><strong>Maintenance note:</strong> this post preserves a compact R Markdown workflow for small GitHub Pages sites. For this blog itself I have since moved to Quarto, which makes project configuration and rendering cleaner, but the original R Markdown approach is still useful for lightweight sites.</p>
<p>Example of one of my GitHub pages:
<img src="https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11966330/110238718-2a8d3180-7f11-11eb-9655-dd6c4a4c5a3b.JPG" /></p>
<p>You might have read this <a href="https://resources.github.com/whitepapers/github-and-rstudio/">GitHub and RStudio</a> tutorial while searching this topic. It is quite long because it teaches Git at the same time. For a small static site, you do not need those branch operations. The example YAML code is also easy to mis-indent, so I corrected it below.</p>
<p><strong>Here is the short version:</strong></p>
<ol style="list-style-type: decimal">
<li>Create in the root directory a yaml file: "_site.yml"</li>
</ol>
<p>Make sure the YAML is indented correctly. Most errors come from malformed <code>.yml</code> files. For example, I get the error “Format is not of class rmarkdown” if I remove one space before <code>theme: cosmo</code>.</p>
<p>The following example as in the tutorial (format corrected) creates a navbar with website title “Cars”, home page named “HomePage” (using <em>index.html</em>) and another page called “Page 1” (using <em>speed-and-distance.html</em>).</p>
<p>The HTML filenames in <code>href</code> should match your R Markdown HTML output. I would usually name the <strong>.Rmd</strong> files with the same base names.</p>
<pre class="r"><code>name: &quot;cars&quot;
output_dir: &quot;docs&quot;
navbar:
  title: &quot;Cars&quot;
  left:
    - text: &quot;HomePage&quot;
      href: index.html
    - text: &quot;Page 1&quot;
      href: speed-and-distance.html
output:
  html_document:
    theme: cosmo</code></pre>
<p>How the navbar on the site looks like
<img src="https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11966330/104111727-a1ac9d80-52b3-11eb-98ae-164eb2d0008e.JPG" /></p>
<p>Here is another example, the yaml file for the sample page posted in the beginning, you can check <a href="https://github.com/liuyanguu/COVerAge_Plot">the repo</a> to see how are the files organized.</p>
<pre class="r"><code>name: &quot;COVerAge_Plot&quot;
output_dir: &quot;docs&quot;
navbar:
  title: &quot;HOME&quot;
  left: 
    - text: &quot;Plots for COVerAGE-DB&quot;
      href: index.html
    - text: &quot;Country profile&quot;
      href: country_report.html
output:
  html_document:
    theme: cosmo</code></pre>
<ol start="2" style="list-style-type: decimal">
<li>Remove the <code>knit</code> and <code>output</code> part from the heading of <strong>.Rmd</strong> files
so they do not need their own <code>output</code> fields anymore.</li>
</ol>
<pre class="r"><code>---
title: &quot;Speed and Distance&quot;
---</code></pre>
<ol start="3" style="list-style-type: decimal">
<li>Render site</li>
</ol>
<p>This will render every <strong>.Rmd</strong> file in the root directory.<br />
Think the GitHub page as a one-page site with index.html as the homepage.</p>
<pre class="r"><code>rmarkdown::render_site()</code></pre>
<ol start="4" style="list-style-type: decimal">
<li>Push to GitHub</li>
</ol>
<p>Make sure the homepage is named <code>index.html</code>. Go to repository settings -&gt; GitHub Pages and point the source to the folder containing this <code>index.html</code> file. You can also change the theme using the “Theme Chooser”.</p>
<div class="figure">
<img src="https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11966330/104090319-f7496180-5243-11eb-91f9-39cf0ddf30ab.JPG" alt="" />
<p class="caption">GitHub Page</p>
</div>
<p>You can only assign the short domain names like <a href="https://liuyanguu.github.io/">liuyanguu.github.io</a> to one repo by changing the name of your repo into this URL (in my case, this blog, I have a repo named <code>liuyanguu.github.io</code>). All the rest pages and sites hosted on GitHub will have the repo name attached behind: <a href="https://liuyanguu.github.io/COVerAge_Plot/">liuyanguu.github.io/COVerAge_Plot</a> (although this is not a page on this blog).</p>
</div>
